headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Kestra can write broad workflow data while Unstructured parses documents, creating default-path exposure and unverified handoff risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and process workflow inputs, logs, and messages; Unstructured reads documents and text. If Kestra passes document content into Unstructured or re-ingests its outputs from shared files, prompt-like instructions embedded in content could influence downstream processing. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF Kestra writes Unstructured-processed documents into a shared workspace without sanitization, THEN embedded instructions can propagate.
IF Unstructured output is later treated as workflow instructions by Kestra, THEN injection risk materializes.
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents.
Strip or escape instruction-like text before handoff.
Require a schema validator on Unstructured outputs.
Use read-only mounts for document inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every file handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Unstructured processes documents, images, and text. A shared filesystem or workspace would let sensitive workflow data flow into document parsing and back out again. No direct evidence of isolation is provided, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same workspace, THEN workflow data can be exposed to document parsing.
IF Kestra writes logs or artifacts into a directory Unstructured reads, THEN sensitive content can leak into outputs.
mitigations: Use separate per-agent workspaces.
Disable shared mounts for logs and artifacts.
Redact secrets before document parsing.
Restrict Unstructured to a narrow input directory.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and spawn subprocesses, and Kestra additionally executes shell commands with broad network egress. If they share a writable directory, concurrent runs can overwrite artifacts or corrupt workflow state. Because no locking or coordination primitive is documented, the overlap is dangerous by default and could cause irreversible pipeline damage.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, THEN file clobbering or partial writes can occur.
IF Kestra shells out while Unstructured writes artifacts concurrently, THEN race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Run one agent at a time on shared resources.
Use file locks around shared paths.
Make shared mounts read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: add transactional artifact writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow artifacts, logs, and notifications that Unstructured may consume as text or documents. If Unstructured treats Kestra output as authoritative without verification, parsing errors or malformed content can cascade into downstream automation. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default orchestration flows, so high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Unstructured consumes Kestra-produced artifacts without validation, THEN bad upstream data can propagate.
IF Kestra notifications are parsed as documents, THEN malformed content can trigger incorrect downstream extraction.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Validate file formats before parsing.
Reject empty or malformed artifacts.
Limit Unstructured to known-safe document types.
requires-engineering: add checksum-based handoff validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra explicitly touches cloud storage data, database data, messages, and notifications, while Unstructured processes documents and text and exposes a privacy-policy endpoint. If regulated or personal data flows through both, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, but they do show enough surface area to justify medium risk.
conditions: IF EU personal data is routed through both agents without a DPA, THEN residency/compliance issues arise.
IF retention policies differ for artifacts and parsed documents, THEN deletion requests may fail end-to-end.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document retention for artifacts and parsed outputs.
Review privacy-policy and storage endpoints before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement deletion propagation across both systems.
